Ana: Heads-up — seeing a 25% p95 latency regression on mixtral-7b-canary when running the multi-turn chat template with ~450-600 tokens of history.
Mike: repro steps? which image/commit?
Ana: canary image rdeploy-2026-03-15, config: batch_size=4, max_new_tokens=128, stream=false. It spikes only when history > ~400 tokens and when the tokenizer emits byte-fallback tokens.
Sasha: curious — do you have a profile?
Ana: pasted flamegraph from the canary run:
```
# perf script condensed
gen_step  | kernel_selector::pick() -> byte_fallback_kernel (nv=1)
gen_step+1| run_byte_kernel_fp32 -> 12.3ms
kv_write  | kv_cache_write -> 0.9ms
kv_read   | kv_cache_lookup -> 1.2ms (misses ~22%)
```
Ana: profiler also shows a kernel switch at the very first token generation after the prompt ends — weird.
Mike: byte_fallback_kernel? that suggests tokenizer produced non-utf8-safe tokenization for some special sequences. which prompts trigger it?
Ana: turns out customer chat templates include emoji shortcodes and an in-house system tag like `<sys:meta>` which gets encoded as bytes by our byte-level fallback path. When that happens the kernel picker prefers the byte-fallback kernel which is much slower on Ampere for these models.
Sasha: also possible RoPE mismatch causing KV key shapes to look incompatible to the optimized kernel, triggering the fallback. heads/kv-dim mismatch?
Rachel: I inspected model config: mixtral-7b variant on canary has 32 heads, kv_dim=128, rope_base=10000, but our kernel heuristics currently check for kv_dim % 64 == 0 and head_count >= 16. That should match, but the picker also checks tokenization.byte_fallback flag and force picks a different kernel if true.
Dino: so two separate levers: (1) tokenizer causes byte_fallback -> slower kernel; (2) KV cache key includes BOS/EOS and some system tags -> cache misses -> more recompute. Combined they amplify latency.
Perf-bot: Incident detected: canary mixtral-7b p95 up 25% over baseline (last 24h).
Mike: quick mitigations?
Sasha: 1) Patch cache key normalization: strip leading BOS and trailing EOS before computing KV cache key, and canonicalize system tags. 2) Short-circuit tokenizer post-processing to avoid byte-fallback for ASCII/Emoji shortcodes we control. 3) Update kernel-picker to prefer rope-optimized kernel when model.rope_base matches known set and (kv_dim % 64 == 0 or heads >= 32).
Rachel: agree. Also add a guard to avoid switching kernels mid-generation unless the model architecture actually changes — we saw a switch at gen step 1 which is expensive. Kernel-switching churn seems costly.
Dino: i can implement the cache-key patch today (PR opened: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2041). Will add unit tests for sample chat templates.
Ana: thanks — after applying local cache-key patch, I reran canary and p95 improved from +25% back to +6%. Still room for kernel-picker tweak.
Mike: Sasha, can you own the kernel-picker heuristic? update will need perf tests across llama/mistral/mixtral/qwen variants.
Sasha: taking it. Plan: add heuristic table prioritized by (tokenizer_fallback, rope_compat, kv_shape). Fallback rule: if tokenizer_fallback==true AND model.rope_compat==true, do NOT select byte-fallback kernel unless no other kernel supports the token type. This prevents accidental preference for slower byte kernels. Will run batch perf matrix tomorrow.
Perf-bot: scheduled perf matrix job: perf-matrix/1849876543-1 queued.
Rachel: small note — we should also log when tokenizer returns byte_fallback and which tokens triggered it (anonymized) so we can catch new templates.
Ana: added a quick logging hook locally; it shows most hits come from `<sys:meta>` + old emoji shortcodes. Rewriting the template to use unicode emoji removed byte fallback entirely for our test cases.
Mike: TL;DR action list:
  - Dino: cache-key normalization patch (in progress).
  - Sasha: kernel-picker heuristic change + perf matrix (owner).
  - Rachel: add telemetry for tokenizer.byte_fallback events and the token types.
  - Ana: run end-to-end canary after above and report p50/p95/p99.
Rachel: ETA for telemetry PR is EOD tomorrow.
Dino: PR link: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2041 — reviewers @sasha @mike
Sasha: starting perf matrix now. Will post summary with numbers and recommended kernel defaults (rope-preferred threshold) in this thread.
Ana: thanks all :thumbsup:
Mike: nice investigation. Once changes land, consider adding an automated canary that injects special tokens and checks for kernel selection stability.
Sasha: good call — adding a canary case to perf suite.
perf-bot: canary job updated: canary/cases/tokenizer-kernel-stability added.
Rachel: :eyes:
Ana: closing loop tomorrow after perf numbers.
Mike: good work — low churn, high impact.
